evals.name: security-secrets-scan
evals.prompt: Run the tenet-security and tenet-secrets skills against this codebase. Scan for injection risks, hardcoded secrets, auth gaps, and CORS issues. Write findings to .healthcheck/reports/security.json and .healthcheck/reports/secrets.json following the Tenet report schema.
evals.expected_output: Two JSON files with scored findings — security should flag any eval/exec usage, SQL injection risks, CORS config; secrets should detect any hardcoded keys or .env patterns. Both must include fix_prompts for every finding.

evals.name: complexity-solid-analysis
evals.prompt: Run the tenet-complexity and tenet-solid skills against this codebase. Measure cyclomatic complexity, function length, file length, and nesting depth. Then evaluate SOLID principle adherence — look for SRP violations, concrete dependencies in business logic, and fat interfaces. Write findings to .healthcheck/reports/complexity.json and .healthcheck/reports/solid.json.
evals.expected_output: Two JSON files. Complexity should flag functions with cyclomatic complexity >10, files >500 lines, functions >50 lines. SOLID should identify god classes or modules with mixed responsibilities. Both must use the scoring formula and include fix_prompts.

evals.name: testing-debt-docs
evals.prompt: Run the tenet-testing, tenet-debt, and tenet-docs skills against this codebase. Evaluate test coverage and quality (look for .only, skipped tests, coverage reports). Scan for aged TODO/FIXME/HACK comments and commented-out code. Check README completeness and inline doc coverage. Write findings to .healthcheck/reports/testing.json, .healthcheck/reports/debt.json, and .healthcheck/reports/docs.json.
evals.expected_output: Three JSON files. Testing should find the e2e test structure and flag any .only or skipped tests. Debt should find and age TODO/FIXME comments via git blame. Docs should evaluate README sections. All must include fix_prompts and use the scoring formula.

evals.name: errors-observability-buildci
evals.prompt: Run the tenet-errors, tenet-observability, and tenet-build-ci skills against this codebase. Check for empty catch blocks, unhandled promise rejections, and missing error boundaries. Evaluate logging patterns, health endpoints, and graceful shutdown. Audit the CI config in .github/workflows/ci.yml for lockfile presence, test steps, and pinned versions. Write findings to .healthcheck/reports/errors.json, .healthcheck/reports/observability.json, and .healthcheck/reports/build-ci.json.
evals.expected_output: Three JSON files. Errors should flag empty catches and broad exception handling. Observability should check for structured logging and health endpoints. Build-CI should audit the GitHub Actions workflow. All must include fix_prompts.

evals.name: performance-deps-api-a11y
evals.prompt: Run the tenet-performance, tenet-dependencies, tenet-api-contract, and tenet-accessibility skills against this codebase. Look for N+1 patterns, memory leaks, and React re-render hazards. Check package.json for outdated or vulnerable dependencies. Evaluate API route consistency if API routes are found. Scan TSX files for missing alt text, ARIA labels, and form label associations. Write findings to .healthcheck/reports/performance.json, .healthcheck/reports/dependencies.json, .healthcheck/reports/api-contract.json, and .healthcheck/reports/accessibility.json. If a dimension is not applicable, set score to null and applicable to false.
evals.expected_output: Four JSON files. Performance should find React hazards in the web app and any N+1 patterns in the API. Dependencies should check package.json health. API contract should evaluate route handlers if present. Accessibility should scan TSX for a11y issues. Each must use the scoring formula and include fix_prompts.

evals.name: ops-privacy-supplychain-infra-db-release
evals.prompt: Run the tenet-privacy-data, tenet-supply-chain-license, tenet-infra-cloud, tenet-database-migrations, and tenet-release-ops skills against this codebase. Classify where personal data lives, inventory personal fields and trace them into logs, analytics and third parties; check deletion coverage, expiry, consent gates and device permissions; SBOM/license/provenance gaps, infrastructure-as-code exposure, migration safety, and release/rollback readiness. Write findings to .healthcheck/reports/privacy-data.json, .healthcheck/reports/supply-chain-license.json, .healthcheck/reports/infra-cloud.json, .healthcheck/reports/database-migrations.json, and .healthcheck/reports/release-ops.json. If a dimension is not applicable, set score to null and applicable to false.
evals.expected_output: Five JSON files. Applicable dimensions should include scored findings with fix_prompts and confidence tiers; non-applicable dimensions should set score to null and applicable to false. All findings must follow the Tenet location contract for file/line and fix_prompt Location. privacy-data.json must state the residency classification in notes, report flows and gaps only (never a bare field or a missing policy), and skip deletion and expiry checks for device-only data. release-ops, supply-chain-license, infra-cloud and database-migrations must state the project scale (solo or team) in notes and report absence-of-process findings as info at solo scale.

evals.name: correctness-logic-bugs
evals.prompt: Run the tenet-correctness skill against this codebase. Select a bounded review set, filling the budget with code that is new, changed or not yet reviewed according to .healthcheck/state/correctness-coverage.json, then read each unit and trace concrete inputs looking for logic bugs. Run the invariant pass over money and status write sites and the variant sweep for each confirmed bug. Carry forward and re-verify findings from the previous correctness.json if one exists. State a concrete failing input for every finding. Write findings to .healthcheck/reports/correctness.json following the Tenet report schema.
evals.expected_output: correctness.json plus an updated .healthcheck/state/correctness-coverage.json. The report must select a bounded review set (not the whole repo) and state which files were and were not reviewed in notes. Every finding must include a concrete 'input X -> wrong output Y' scenario, a snippet, and a fix_prompt. Metrics must include invariants_checked, variant_sweeps and carried_forward. Variants of one root cause are folded into one finding that lists every file:line. Must use the scoring formula and honor suppressions.

evals.name: security-fixture-recall
evals.prompt: Run the tenet-security skill against the evals/fixtures/security-recall/ directory as the project root. Build the entry-point inventory, scan every vulnerability class, and run the mandatory verification pass. Write findings to .healthcheck/reports/security.json. Then score with: python3 evals/score-fixtures.py --expected evals/fixtures/security-recall/EXPECTED.json --report .healthcheck/reports/security.json
evals.expected_output: security.json plus a passing score run: recall >= 80% of the 23 planted vulnerabilities across all classes (SQL/command/XSS/NoSQL injection, IDOR, tenant isolation, mass assignment, path traversal, JWT alg-none, timing-unsafe compare, weak hashing, weak random, SSRF, CORS, unverified webhook, prototype pollution, zip-slip, default creds, unsafe yaml.load, mobile insecure storage, unvalidated root XPC listener, hardlink-redirectable root file op, DNS-rebindable localhost server) AND zero false positives on the 12 safe decoys (parameterized query, Drizzle sql tagged template, DOMPurify-wrapped HTML, execFile array, Math.random jitter, sha1 cache key, ownership-scoped query, publishable Stripe key, allowlisted SSRF, Team-ID-pinned XPC requirement, Host-checked loopback server without token, same-user subprocess).

evals.name: correctness-fixture-recall
evals.prompt: Copy evals/fixtures/correctness-recall/project/ to a scratch directory, make it a git repository, and run the tenet-correctness skill with that directory as the project root. Do not read evals/fixtures/correctness-recall/EXPECTED.json. Write findings to .healthcheck/reports/correctness.json. Then score with: python3 evals/score-fixtures.py --expected evals/fixtures/correctness-recall/EXPECTED.json --report <scratch>/.healthcheck/reports/correctness.json
evals.expected_output: correctness.json plus a passing score run: recall >= 80% of the 13 planted bugs (missing await, check-then-act race, pagination off-by-one and its variant in a second endpoint, refunds that can exceed the charge, webhook credited twice on redelivery, refund before non-transactional writes, inverted session expiry, copy-paste zip, null dereference of a soft-deleted user, quantity 0 coerced to 1, dollars passed where cents are expected, stock decremented below zero) AND zero false positives on the 11 decoys (atomic conditional update, correct 1-based pagination, deduped webhook, sequential retry backoff, correct expiry check, validated and null-guarded lookup, dead code, integer-cents rounding, intended rounding asserted by a test, guarded stock write, increment-only write).

evals.name: privacy-fixture-recall
evals.prompt: Copy evals/fixtures/privacy-recall/project/ to a scratch directory, make it a git repository, and run the tenet-privacy-data skill with that directory as the project root. Do not read evals/fixtures/privacy-recall/EXPECTED.json. Write findings to .healthcheck/reports/privacy-data.json. Then score with: python3 evals/score-fixtures.py --expected evals/fixtures/privacy-recall/EXPECTED.json --report <scratch>/.healthcheck/reports/privacy-data.json
evals.expected_output: privacy-data.json plus a passing score run: recall >= 80% of the 10 planted issues (request logger dumping bodies and auth headers, signup logging name/email/phone, card details attached to an error report, email and name sent to analytics identify, full user record posted to a chat webhook, account deletion that leaves sessions and uploads, reset tokens that never expire, analytics that ignores the opt-out setting, email in a query string, location API with no purpose string) AND zero false positives on the 8 decoys (opaque-ID log, email provider receiving the address it needs, redacting logger, model types, schema fields, a declared camera permission, test data, the settings module).
